  Social Network Analysis [IT_4411]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                In the graph in Figure 1a, node B is pivotal for two pairs: the pair consisting of A and C, and the pair (2)  
  consisting of A and D. (Notice that B is not pivotal for the pair consisting of D and E since there are  
  A)           two different shortest paths connecting D and E, one of which (using C and F) doesn't pass through  
  B. So B is not on every shortest path between D and E.) On the other hand, node D is not pivotal  
  for any pairs.  
  (a) Construct a graph in which every node is pivotal for at least one pair of nodes. Explain your  
  answer.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           In a large healthcare organization, a social network of doctors, nurses, and administrative staff is     (4)  
  mapped to understand communication patterns. It is observed that:  
  
  Doctors mostly interact with other doctors.  
  Nurses communicate frequently within their own group.  
  A few nurses act as links between doctors and administrative staff.  
  There are strong triadic connections within each department (i.e., if A knows B and B knows  
  C, then A often knows C)  
  
  Analyze how transitivity within the doctor network might enhance trust and coordination but  
  potentially limit information diversity  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"

2)        In the social network depicted in Figure 2a, with each edge labeled as either a strong or weak tie,    (5)  
  which nodes satisfy the Strong Triadic Closure Property, and which do not? Justify your answer.  
  A)

  B)   Given a network showing pairs of people who share activities, we can try to reconstruct an affiliation (5)  
  network consistent with this data. For example, suppose that you are trying to infer the structure of  
  a bipartite affiliation network, and by indirect observation you've obtained the projected network on  
  just the set of people, there is an edge joining each pair of people who share a focus. This projected  
  network is shown in Figure 2b.  
  (i) Determine an affiliation network involving these six people, together with four foci that you  
  should define, whose projected network is the graph shown in Figure 2b.  
  (ii) Justify why any affiliation network capable of producing the projected network in Figure 2b must  
  have at least four foci.
